knowledge-heavy.label: Knowledge / recall
knowledge-heavy.guidance: Test definitions, terminology, classifications, ordering of steps, and properties stated directly in the section. Distractors must be adjacent terms from this same section that a student who half-learned the material would confuse with the correct one — never invented jargon.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.guidance: Mix definitional questions with situations that require applying a rule. Roughly half the questions should be answerable only by someone who understands the mechanism, not just its name.

scenario-heavy.label: Scenario / application
scenario-heavy.guidance: Every stem is a concrete situation with specific conditions or values. The student must trace a mechanism, predict an outcome, or choose the correct action. No question may be answerable by recognizing a definition. Vary the scenarios — do not reuse the same setup with different numbers.

calculation.label: Numeric / calculation
calculation.guidance: Numeric problems solvable in under two minutes without a calculator where possible. Each distractor must be the result of one specific plausible error — a unit slip, an off-by-one, a swapped numerator/denominator, applying the wrong formula — and whyWrong must name that error. Never use random numbers as distractors.

compare-contrast.label: Compare / contrast
compare-contrast.guidance: Focus on distinguishing similar concepts, protocols, algorithms, or categories covered in the section: which one applies, how they differ, what trade-off each makes. Distractors are the sibling concepts themselves.
